title: Sepsis, severe sepsis, septic shock, urosepsis and bacteremia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the sepsis, severe sepsis or septic shock only (not the local infection or the organ dysfunction). If none applies, choose 'no code'.
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Sepsis from skin infection

Vitals: BP 118/74, HR 88, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 99.1 F.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Positive for fever, chills, and malaise.
Integumentary: Positive for localized erythema and warmth of a skin lesion.
Respiratory: Negative for cough or shortness of breath.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain or palpitations.
Genitourinary: Negative for dysuria.

HPI: Patient is a 58-year-old woman who presented with a rapidly progressing skin infection on her left forearm. She reports increased pain, swelling, and drainage. She describes feeling systemically ill with tremors and fatigue over the last 48 hours.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for sepsis originating from a localized skin infection. Cultures were positive for MSSA. She showed no signs of acute organ dysfunction during her stay. She was treated with cefazolin intravenously for the methicillin-sensitive infection. She responded well to antibiotics, with clinical improvement and stabilization of vital signs.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Sepsis due to methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) from a skin infection.

Discharge Medications:
Cefazolin 750mg every 8 hours (transition to oral)
Ibuprofen 400mg every 6 hours as needed for pain.

Follow-up:
Follow up with primary care physician in 7 days for wound assessment.

Electronically signed, K. Nguyen, MD, 05/15/2026
explanations: Sepsis due to methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus: A41.01 (HCC 2).
